solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: going round in a circle: the first letter of SIS rides round to the end
the cycled sibling sits inside the word for dark

blocks.note: dismal = dark, gloomy; it is split to hold the sibling
SIS (sister) with its first S sent round to the back

annotation.surface: A notice pinned up about a brother or sister out cycling after dark.
annotation.walkthrough: A notice here is notice to quit a job, so the answer is the sacking, not a sign on a wall.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the employment sense: being given notice means being sacked.

indicators.note: what you pocket you hold inside, so the word for stooping takes in the S

blocks.note: to deign = to stoop to doing something
s = shilling, from the old British £sd currency

annotation.surface: A sly figure bending down to slip a coin into a pocket.
annotation.walkthrough: Stooping is the social sense, lowering yourself to do something, not bending over.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a scheming, artful person is described with this participle, as in a designing woman.

entries.clue: Scathing contempt, often really nasty initially (5)

definitions.text: Scathing contempt, often really nasty initially

indicators.note: at the start of each word, so take every first letter

blocks.note: first letters of Scathing, Contempt, Often, Really, Nasty

annotation.surface: A remark that contempt usually comes out nasty.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its initials spell the answer, and read straight it describes the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: contempt of this kind is scathing and often nasty.

entries.clue: Protected shell’s mouth with hardened exterior (7)

indicators.note: the mouth is the opening, so the first letter of shell
the outside, so the word for hardened wraps around the S

annotation.surface: A shellfish protected by its tough outer casing.
annotation.walkthrough: Shell, mouth and hardened exterior all conjure a crab or mussel; protected is the insurance kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Synonym through cover: a policy protects you against loss, so a covered house is protected.

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover all round, so the outer words dress the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words: the end of polyester and the start of lingerie

annotation.surface: A complaint that synthetic underwear is passed off as the real thing.
annotation.walkthrough: Clothes looks like a noun in a clue about lingerie, but it is a verb: the phrase clothes the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense from the silver standard: genuine, of proven quality.

entries.clue: Boys spending penny once in toilet (6)

indicators.note: what you spend you give away, so the boys part with their penny

blocks.note: laddies = boys; the D between LAD and IES is removed
d = penny in pre-1971 British money

annotation.surface: Boys once paid a penny to use the toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: To spend a penny is British slang for going to the toilet, from the old coin-operated locks, so the surface is a joke about the very place the answer names.
annotation.definitionFit: British idiom: the women's public toilet, as a sign on a door would name it.

entries.clue: Catwalks? Viewed regularly, they can bore (4)

indicators.note: looked at at regular intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

annotation.surface: Fashion shows: watched often enough, they become tedious.
annotation.walkthrough: Bore reads as tedium after catwalks, but it means drill.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: these pointed hand tools pierce, or bore, holes in leather and wood.

indicators.note: without an end, so the word loses its final letter
to preserve is to keep safe inside, so the shortened word holds the jams

blocks.note: a jam or a hole = a tight spot, trouble

annotation.surface: Decent ladies forever making preserves.
annotation.walkthrough: Preserving and jams paint a kitchen, but jams are predicaments, and preserving means holding inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: morally sound and respectable, as in good clean family fun.

entries.clue: Disapproving sounds raised about Queen’s parade (5)

indicators.note: lifted up, and in a down clue that means read from bottom to top
around, so the reversed word goes around the R

annotation.surface: People tutting loudly at a royal procession.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for is, joining the wordplay to parade, which is a verb rather than the royal procession.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the verb: to walk with a proud, showy gait.

entries.clue: Plate of chicken possibly sent back (6)

indicators.note: returned the way it came, so read backwards

blocks.note: a chicken is one example of an animal

annotation.surface: A restaurant diner returning a plate of chicken.
annotation.walkthrough: Plate of chicken is a dinner order, but plate is the definition and 'of' only links it.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical synonym: a thin layer or plate, as of bone or metal.

indicators.note: going back the way it came, so read backwards

annotation.surface: A skin cream advertisement: keeps pimples from coming back.
annotation.walkthrough: The advertising reading makes returning sound like acne recurring; it is an instruction to reverse.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the verb sense: halts, keeps something from happening.

indicators.note: as reported, by word of mouth, so the word for always is heard not spelt
at the back, so it comes after the target

blocks.note: an end = an aim or target
ever = always; spoken, it matches the last syllables

annotation.surface: A political jibe that the Labour Party always seems to be missing its targets.
annotation.walkthrough: Labour with a capital looks like the British party; here it is hard work.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to labour at something is to strive or try hard.

indicators.note: standing in front of, so the classes come before the L

blocks.note: L = learner, from the L-plate on British learner drivers' cars

annotation.surface: A comprehensive school with classes waiting for a new pupil.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a comprehensive is a state secondary school, which is the picture; the answer uses the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: broad, all-embracing, as in a general knowledge quiz.

entries.clue: Demanding former partner with single bloke (7)

indicators.note: together with, so the pieces are set side by side

annotation.surface: A needy ex who has taken up with an unattached man.
annotation.walkthrough: Single suggests an unattached bloke, but it only gives the numeral I.
annotation.definitionFit: Formal synonym: pressing, requiring much, as in exigent circumstances.

indicators.note: to oust is to throw out, so the R is removed

annotation.surface: A brash, foolish politician who got a Republican thrown out.
annotation.walkthrough: Bold and unwise reads as a pair of adjectives; only bold is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: cheeky, brazen, showing a lack of respect.

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so the prudes hold the ROT

annotation.surface: Straitlaced Victorians covering up what shows under their clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is prim Victorians hiding bulges; degenerate is a verb here, not a noun for a rake.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: sticks out beyond a surface.

entries.clue: Audibly approved for all to hear (5)

indicators.note: in a way that can be heard, so the word for approved is heard not spelt

annotation.surface: A proposal passed out loud, publicly.
annotation.walkthrough: Both ends of the clue speak of hearing, so it is hard to tell which half is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Adverb synonym: out loud, so that everyone present can hear.

entries.clue: Vandal almost wild besieging ancient city (9)

indicators.note: not quite all, so the last letter goes
an army besieging a city surrounds it, so the shortened word goes around TROY

blocks.note: DESERT (a wild, a wilderness) without its last letter
the city besieged by the Greeks

annotation.surface: A barbarian horde laying siege to an old city.
annotation.walkthrough: Wild is a noun, a wilderness; besieging suits the picture since Troy was the most famous siege of all.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: one who wrecks, as the Vandals sacked Rome.

indicators.note: on the inside of, so the ones sit within the pubs

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one, so Is are ones

annotation.surface: A question whether the inside of a pub smells foul.
annotation.walkthrough: Rank looks like an adjective meaning smelly; it is a noun, a title. Is is not the verb but the plural of the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a title in the British peerage, the female equivalent of a baron.

annotation.surface: Fine behinds that make people turn red.
annotation.walkthrough: Bottoms plays on backsides; it means low points.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: a face that reddens shines warmly.

entries.clue: Small containers containing ale, ultimately? No! (6)

definitions.text: Small containers containing ale, ultimately? No!

indicators.note: holding inside, so the tins hold the E
at the very end, so the last letter of ale

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
last letter of ale, which goes inside TINS

annotation.surface: Are beer mugs small? No!
annotation.walkthrough: Read straight, the clue describes the answer and then corrects itself: these containers do hold ale, but the 'No!' insists they are not small.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: large German-style beer mugs are containers of ale, and anything but small.

entries.clue: Tame House’s opening missing some members? (8)

indicators.note: the opening of a word is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: members = limbs; lacking arms is missing some

annotation.surface: A feeble House of Commons with many MPs absent.
annotation.walkthrough: Members suggests MPs in a House; here they are limbs.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: gentle, posing no danger, as a tame animal does.

indicators.note: the fellow takes the kiss prisoner, holding it inside
without a top, and in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A painter's companion catching a model kissing with no top on.
annotation.walkthrough: Topless sounds risqué beside an artist, but it just takes the top letter off smooch's synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Henri, the French painter of bright Fauvist colour.

entries.clue: Like bride groom, forgetting occasion, held? (6)

indicators.note: what you forget you leave out, so the word for occasion is dropped

blocks.note: GROOM without ROOM (room = occasion, as in no room for doubt)

annotation.surface: A groom who forgot the wedding: is it held?
annotation.walkthrough: Occasion suggests the wedding; it means room, as in no occasion or room for complaint.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: dressed in a long formal dress, as a bride is on her wedding day.

indicators.note: to seize is to grab hold, so the split word takes the P inside

annotation.surface: Shock news: a split political party grabs power.
annotation.walkthrough: Divided party reads as one phrase, a split party; divided and party are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: The literal sense of bombshell: a self-propelled underwater explosive shell.

blocks.note: the surface reading: a person behaving in a certain way
the setter's reading: insulting in the virtual world, online, rather than almost insulting

annotation.surface: Someone who is being all but rude.
annotation.walkthrough: Virtually reads as nearly; it means in the virtual world, online.
annotation.definitionFit: Internet slang: a person who posts deliberately provocative insults online.

indicators.note: later in order, so OR is written after OUTDO
vacating a house empties it, so the word is emptied of its middle letters

blocks.note: occupier emptied, leaving only its outer letters

annotation.surface: An eviction: beat the tenant who stayed on after the holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: Vacation looks like a holiday; it is the act of vacating, emptying the word.
annotation.definitionFit: Italian borrowing: alfresco means in the fresh air, open-air.

indicators.note: sitting on top of, and in a down clue that puts OR above LOP

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, ordinary sailors or soldiers
to dock = to cut off, lop

annotation.surface: Sailors on a ship's deck while it is in dock.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is nautical, but dock is a verb, to cut short, as with a dog's tail.
annotation.definitionFit: Nautical term: the lowest deck of a sailing warship.

indicators.note: to house is to hold inside, so the phrase contains the answer

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of record, through in, into the start of ancestral

annotation.surface: A legal register kept in stately family homes.
annotation.walkthrough: Houses looks like part of the noun phrase ancestral houses; it is a verb, containing the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an authoritative order or decree, especially a local by-law.

indicators.note: comes after, so the ally is written after the S
the first letter of Stonewall

annotation.surface: A Confederate soldier following Stonewall Jackson's first attack.
annotation.walkthrough: Stonewall Jackson was a Confederate general in the American Civil War, so the picture is historical; confederate is just an ally.
annotation.definitionFit: Military synonym: a sudden charge out of a besieged position.

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, the middle letter of sweet
not quite all of it, so the last letter goes
sent back, so the pieces are read backwards

annotation.surface: A spurned lover left almost on their own.
annotation.walkthrough: Sweetheart is the middle of sweet, not a lover.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to fail to catch a train, or to fail to win.

blocks.note: complaint in its medical sense, an illness, not a grumble
a setter is a breed of gun dog, not the puzzle's compiler

annotation.surface: A grumble that might put a crossword setter in a bad mood.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter seems to be the crossword's author; it is the dog. There is also a hint of dis-temper, bad temper.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a viral disease of dogs, and a setter is a breed of dog.
